name: A Humble Task
summary: In Red Cloud Mesa, A Humble Task sends young tauren to carry well water to Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks for this service, a first lesson in humility and care for the tribe.

sections.title: Vitality of the Youth
sections.body: Greatmother Hawkwind has walked many trails, though age has slowed her across the plains. She tends to her duties beside the well on Red Cloud Mesa's southern edge. When young tauren with hopes of defending their people meet her, she turns their energy toward the needs of the community. Service gives them a chance to prove themselves through care for others.

sections.title: Service to the Tribe
sections.body: You carry a filled pitcher northwest to Camp Narache and give it to Chief Hawkwind, the settlement's leader and Greatmother Hawkwind's son. Life across Mulgore's dry plains depends on shared labor and steady supplies of fresh water. By carrying a burden for an elder, you show respect for the people whose care holds the tribe together.

sections.title: A Path Toward Thunder Bluff
sections.body: When you bring his mother's water to Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sees more than a chore completed. Tauren custom asks those who would champion their people across distant lands to begin with humility and a ready hand. Your quiet discipline catches the chief's eye, and he recommends you for the Rites of the Earthmother, spiritual tests that open the gates to Thunder Bluff.

faq.answer: Greatmother Hawkwind is an elder of the Hawkwind family who tends the well on Red Cloud Mesa. She is Chief Hawkwind's mother and teaches young tauren humility and care for their tribe.

faq.q: Where is the water well located?
faq.answer: The water well is southeast of Camp Narache, on the grassy plains of Red Cloud Mesa. Pitchers of fresh water rest beside it for travelers and camp caretakers to carry back.
Chief Hawkwind leads Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. He directs the training and spiritual rites of young tauren as they prepare to serve the wider tribe in Mulgore.

faq.q: Why is this chore treated as an important test?
faq.answer: Tauren value humility, care for the community, and respect for elders. Everyday duties show that you care for your people as well as your own glory in battle.

faq.q: What comes after completing A Humble Task?
faq.answer: After carrying the water, Chief Hawkwind directs you to the Rites of the Earthmother, traditional challenges for tauren coming of age.

faq.q: Where does this path eventually lead?
faq.answer: The elders' respect prepares you to leave Red Cloud Mesa and travel across Mulgore toward Thunder Bluff, the capital's high mesas.

angles.text: As a tauren, carrying water for your elders shows communal care and readiness to walk the path of the Earthmother.
As a member of the Horde, you see how the Hawkwind family teaches tauren solidarity and survival in Mulgore, a peaceful yet steadfast part of Thrall's Horde.
